ThirdPartyVoter\n///         implementation. Pool gauges and validator gauges stay on veBTC.\n/// @dev The upgrade transaction must be carefully prepared and executed outside\n///      of the epoch distribution window:\n///      0. Ensure there are no whitelisted NFTs in the voter - check\n///         `isWhitelistedNFT(uint256)` so that veBTC identifiers are not\n///         representing veMEZO identifiers.\n///      1. Enumerate the veBTC token ids that currently hold a vote, by reading\n///         `usedWeights(tokenId)`. You will need to pass this list as a\n///         parameter.\n///      2. `distribute(gauges)` for every live gauge, so that the emissions\n///         already allocated to them land in the gauges.\n\n///      3. `killThirdPartyGauge(thirdParty)` for every live gauge.\n///      4. `ProxyAdmin.upgradeAndCall(proxy, thisImplementation, data)` where\n///         `data` is `abi.encodeCall(migrateVe, (veMEZO, tokenIds))` and the\n///         value is zero.\n///      5. `ProxyAdmin.upgradeAndCall(proxy, regularThirdPartyVoter, \"\")` to\n///         drop this implementation.\n///      6. `veMEZO.addSecondaryVoter(thirdPartyVoter)` to register this voter\n///         in veMEZO.\n///      7. `createThirdPartyGauge` for at least one replacement gauge, and cast\n///         a vote on it before the next epoch flip.\n/// @custom:oz-upgrades-unsafe-allow missing-initializer\ncontract ThirdPartyVoterVeMigration is ThirdPartyVoter {\n    /// @dev EIP-1967 admin slot,\n    ///      `bytes32(uint256(keccak256(\"eip1967.proxy.admin\")) - 1)`.\n    bytes32 private constant ADMIN_SLOT =\n        0xb53127684a568b3173ae13b9f8a6016e243e63b6e8ee1178d6a717850b5d6103;\n\n    /// @notice Emitted once the voting escrow has been switched.\n    event VeMigrated(address indexed veBTC, address indexed veMEZO);\n\n    /// @notice Thrown when the caller is not the proxy admin, i.e. the call did\n    ///         not come from `upgradeAndCall`.\n    error NotProxyAdmin();\n\n    /// @notice Thrown when votes are still outstanding after the reset pass.\n    error WeightsNotCleared();\n\n    /// @notice Thrown when a gauge has not been killed before the switch.\n    error GaugeStillAlive(address gauge);\n\n    /// @custom:oz-upgrades-unsafe-allow constructor\n    constructor(address _forwarder) ThirdPartyVoter(_forwarder) {}\n\n    /// @notice Unwinds every outstanding veBTC vote, then switches the voter\n    ///         over to veMEZO.\n    /// @param veMEZO The veMEZO voting escrow of the target network.\n    /// @param tokenIds Every veBTC token id that currently holds a vote in this\n    ///        voter. An incomplete list leaves weight behind and reverts the\n    ///        whole call, which is the intended failure mode.\n    /// @dev Callable exactly once, and only from `upgradeAndCall`. Unwind while `ve` still points at veBTC, so the\n        // `voting(tokenId, false)` calls land there and the bribe withdrawals\n        // hit the bribes that actually hold the balances.\n        uint256 tokenCount = tokenIds.length;\n        for (uint256 i = 0; i < tokenCount; i++) {\n            uint256 tokenId = tokenIds[i];\n            _reset(tokenId);\n            // `_reset(tokenId)` does not clear `lastVoted[tokenId]`. We could\n            // leave the existing values, as the timestamps only ever increase,\n            // but after killing the gauges and replacing the voting escrow they\n            // no longer mean anything.\n            delete lastVoted[tokenId];\n        }\n\n        // Step 2. Refuse to proceed with any weight left over, the backstop\n        // against an incomplete `tokenIds` list, or with any gauge still alive.\n        if (totalWeight != 0) revert WeightsNotCleared();\n        uint256 gaugeCount = gauges.length;\n        for (uint256 i = 0; i < gaugeCount; i++) {\n            address gauge = gauges[i];\n            if (weights[gauge] != 0) revert WeightsNotCleared();\n            if (isAlive[gauge]) revert GaugeStillAlive(gauge);\n        }\n\n        // Step 3. Switch the escrow as the last step. A handful of references to\n        // veBTC survive in state afterwards, all of them harmless:\n        // * `gauges[]` keeps the killed gauges forever, and each of those has a\n        //   `Gauge.ve` immutable still reading veBTC.\n        // * `gaugeToBribe[killedGauge]` still points at a veBTC-bound bribe,\n        //   unreachable now that the gauge is dead.\n        // * `veBTC.secondaryVoters[thisVoter]` stays true, as the escrow has no\n        //   remove function.
